questions.stem: An HR Admin without the System Admin role can do what? (Choose three.)

options.text: Grant roles to users or groups

questions.explanation: An HR Admin (without System Admin) can modify HR Administration Properties (B), create HR Criteria (D), and add users to groups (F). Granting roles requires user_admin (A), resetting passwords requires admin/password_reset (C), and configuring business rules requires admin/delegated_developer in global scope (E). HR Admin has group membership management but not role/password management.

questions.stem: After the HR Admin [sn_hr_core.admin] role has been removed from the Admin role, how may a user with only the Admin role add members to HR groups?

options.text: The Admin must elevate their role to security_admin to add members to HR groups.
The Admin follows the same process as with any group membership change.
The Admin can no longer add members to HR groups.
The Admin must impersonate an HR Admin to add members to HR groups.

questions.explanation: When the sn_hr_core.admin role is removed from the Admin role, the System Admin loses the ability to manage HR group membership. HR groups are scoped to the HR application, so without the HR Admin role, the Admin cannot add members to HR groups. Elevating to security_admin (A) does not grant HR-scoped group management, and impersonation (D) is not the correct approach.

questions.stem: In the Create Bulk Cases module, which Filter by options are available in the dropdown? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The Create Bulk Cases module Filter by dropdown offers: Upload File (B) to import a CSV, User Criteria (D) to filter by user attributes, HR Profiles (F) to filter by profile attributes, and HR Criteria (G) to filter employees by HR-specific criteria. Document Template (A), HR Service Template (C), and HR Template (E) are not filter options in the bulk case creation module.

questions.stem: If you have both Admin and HR Admin roles and wanted to configure an Access Control for the Employee Relations Cases table, what must first be done?

options.text: Add the Delegated Developer role to your User record
From the User dropdown in the banner, elevate your role to security_admin
Manually add the security_admin role to your User record
Nothing would need to be done

questions.explanation: To configure Access Control Lists (ACLs) in ServiceNow, you must elevate to security_admin from the user dropdown in the banner. Even with both Admin and HR Admin roles, ACL configuration requires the elevated security_admin role. This is a platform-level security measure that applies regardless of whether you are working with HR tables or any other tables.

questions.stem: What type of information does the HR Profile contain?
questions.explanation: The HR Profile [sn_hr_core_profile] table stores personal employee data such as marital status, emergency contacts, and other HR-specific confidential information. It is separate from the User [sys_user] table which stores login credentials, group memberships, and department info. The HR Profile is specifically designed to hold sensitive personal data that HR needs to manage.

questions.stem: How many User Criteria Records may be applied to a single KB or KB Article?
questions.explanation: There is no limit to the number of User Criteria records that can be applied to a Knowledge Base or Knowledge Article. Multiple Can Read and Cannot Read user criteria records can be configured to control access granularly. This applies equally to KB-level and article-level user criteria settings.

questions.stem: In the base ServiceNow instance, how are User Criteria used?

options.text: To control which users can access the HR Case application
To control what a user sees in the information and suggested reading widgets
To control read and write access to Knowledge bases and articles
To control which users can access the HR Service Portal

questions.explanation: In the base ServiceNow instance, User Criteria controls read and write access to Knowledge Bases and Knowledge articles through Can Read, Cannot Read, Can Contribute, and Cannot Contribute settings. HR Criteria (not User Criteria) controls HR-specific content like Employee Service Center visibility. User Criteria is a platform-level feature for knowledge management access control.

questions.stem: Which of the following are true for an HR application as it relates to the User [sys_user] Table and the HR Profile [sn_hr_core.profile] Table?

options.text: Only HR Profile table is required in HR.
Only the User table is required in HR.

questions.explanation: Both the User [sys_user] table and the HR Profile [sn_hr_core_profile] table are required for the HR application. The User table provides the base identity (login, department, groups), and the HR Profile extends this with HR-specific confidential data. An HR Profile references a User record, so both must exist. The HR Profile cannot function without its associated User record.

questions.stem: In the base instance, what determines the conditions a Case must meet before it can be assigned to an agent?
questions.explanation: Matching Rules determine the conditions an HR Case must meet before it can be assigned to an agent. They evaluate case attributes (such as location, COE, skills) and match them against agent qualifications to determine eligible assignees. Assignment Rules (D) actually assign the case, but Matching Rules define the prerequisite conditions. Client Rules and ACLs serve different purposes entirely.

questions.stem: What role is required, at a minimum, to view confidential HR Profile data?
questions.explanation: The HR Basic [sn_hr_core.basic] role is the minimum role required to view confidential HR Profile data. This role is granted to all HR support staff and provides read access to HR profiles including confidential fields. HR Admin (A) and HR Manager (D) also have access but are not the minimum. LE Admin (C) is for lifecycle events, not profile access.

questions.stem: What types of HR Document templates may be created in ServiceNow? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: ServiceNow supports two types of HR Document Templates: Document Templates (A), which are HTML-based templates created within ServiceNow, and PDF document templates (C), which use pre-existing PDF forms with field mappings. Word document templates (B) and text document templates (D) are not available as HR document template types in the platform.

questions.stem: What are the advantages of removing the HR Admin role from the system Admin role after the HR Implementation tasks have been completed? (Choose two.)

options.text: This ensures that HR has control over further HR configurations.
The HR Admin role should remain a part of the system Admin role.
This ensures that confidential HR data is only accessible to users with an HR role.
It is not necessary because the system Admin always has access to all HR data.

questions.explanation: Removing HR Admin from the system Admin role after implementation ensures that HR has control over further HR configurations (A) and that confidential HR data is only accessible to users with an HR role (C). Since HRSD is a scoped application, removing the HR Admin role from Admin prevents unauthorized access to sensitive employee data and gives HR autonomy over their application.

questions.stem: What does ServiceNow now call the HR application?
questions.explanation: ServiceNow's HR application is officially called HRSD — HR Service Delivery. This encompasses the full suite of HR capabilities including case management, lifecycle events, employee center, document management, and integrations. The other options (HRDS, HRSM, HRMS) are not ServiceNow product names.

questions.stem: What defines an employee's access to the HR Service Portal / Employee Service Center?
questions.explanation: Client Roles define an employee's access to the HR Service Portal / Employee Service Center. Client Roles are automatically assigned based on the employee's employment type when their HR Profile is created or modified. These roles (such as new_hire, employee, alumni, contingent) determine what content and services the employee can see on the portal.

questions.stem: What kind of records do HR Requests create?
questions.explanation: HR Requests create HR Cases. When an employee submits a request through the Employee Service Center or an HR professional creates one manually, the system generates an HR Case record in the sn_hr_core_case table. HR Cases are the core work unit in HRSD for tracking and resolving employee requests.

questions.stem: In the HR Guided Setup Module, why are some tasks locked in the Task view?

options.text: They require an elevated role to access.
They are deprecated tasks that should not be completed.
They require other tasks to be completed first.
They require a plugin to be activated first.

questions.explanation: In the HR Guided Setup Module, tasks are locked because they require a plugin to be activated first. The Guided Setup presents tasks in a logical order, and certain tasks depend on specific plugins being active before they can be configured. Once the required plugin is activated, the locked task becomes available.

questions.stem: Which of the following are examples of HR application scopes? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The HR application scopes include: Human Resources: Core (B) for base HR case management, Human Resources: Integrations (D) for third-party system connections, Human Resources: Lifecycle Events (E) for onboarding/transitions, and Human Resources: Service Portal (G) for the Employee Service Center. COE (A) is a concept not an app scope, Knowledge (C) and Global (F) are not HR application scopes.

questions.stem: How can an HR Administrator or Content writer limit which employees will see content on the Employee Service Center?

options.text: All employees will see the same information
Client roles automatically limit what is visible to employees

questions.explanation: HR Criteria is used to limit which employees see content on the Employee Service Center. HR Criteria evaluates HR-specific attributes from the HR Profile (such as department, location, employment type) to control content visibility. User Criteria (C) controls Knowledge Base access, not ESC content. HR Criteria is the HR-specific mechanism for content targeting on the portal.

questions.stem: If the Audience field has been configured on a Lifecycle Event Activity, what will the system do if the subject person does not meet the criteria for that Activity?

options.text: the activity must be manually closed by the HR professional
the Lifecycle Event will be canceled
the activity must be manually closed by the Subject person

questions.explanation: If the Audience field is configured on a Lifecycle Event Activity and the subject person does not meet the audience criteria, the activity will be skipped automatically. The system evaluates audience conditions when processing the lifecycle event, and non-matching activities are simply not created for that person. The lifecycle event itself continues normally.

questions.stem: The ServiceNow SIM methodology is based around what generic methodologies?
questions.explanation: The ServiceNow SIM (ServiceNow Implementation Methodology) is based around Agile and Waterfall methodologies. It combines iterative Agile practices with structured Waterfall planning to provide a hybrid approach suitable for ServiceNow implementations. This allows for flexibility while maintaining the project structure needed for enterprise deployments.

questions.stem: If an HR Services needs to be accessible to employees on the Employee Service Center, what field must be completed on the HR Service?
questions.explanation: For an HR Service to be accessible to employees on the Employee Service Center, the Record Producer field must be completed. The Record Producer is the catalog item that creates the user-facing form employees use to submit requests. Without a Record Producer, the HR Service exists only for internal HR use and is not visible on the employee self-service portal.

questions.stem: HR Profiles may be created for multiple employees using conditions and criteria in which module?
questions.explanation: The Generate HR Profiles module allows HR Profiles to be created for multiple employees using conditions and criteria. Administrators navigate to HR Profile > Generate HR Profiles, set filter conditions to identify target users, select the profile type, and click Create Profiles. This bulk creation is more efficient than creating individual profiles.

questions.stem: User authentication and Instance restriction are examples of what type of security?
questions.explanation: User authentication and instance restriction are examples of Platform Access security. Platform Access is one of the three primary security aspects in ServiceNow (along with Roles/Groups and Contextual Security via ACLs). Platform Access controls who can connect to the instance through mechanisms like user authentication, IP restrictions, and SSO configuration.

questions.stem:
If the HR Service does not have any Case options specified, HR Documents must be manually generated for the HR Case.
In this situation, who is able to generate an HR document for the Case?
questions.explanation: When an HR Service has no Case options specified and HR Documents must be manually generated, only the Assigned to person on the HR Case can generate the document. This ensures that document generation is controlled by the agent responsible for the case, maintaining accountability and preventing unauthorized document creation.

questions.stem: When does the HR Template populate information on the HR Case form?

options.text: When the Opened for person is selected
When the Assignment group is selected.
When the HR Case Type is selected.
When the HR service is selected on the HR Case Creation form.

questions.explanation: The HR Template populates information on the HR Case form when the HR Service is selected during case creation. The HR Service record references an HR Template, and selecting the service triggers the template to auto-fill fields like assignment group, skills, priority, and other case attributes. This happens at service selection, not when the opened-for person is chosen.

questions.stem: The HR Profile table is used to track information for what Employment types? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The HR Profile table tracks information for three employment types: Full Time Employee (C), Temporary Employee (D), and Contractor (F). These represent the standard workforce categories that HR manages. Potential Employee (B) is not a standard employment type tracked by HR Profiles, and Spouse (E) and Other (A) are not employment types in the HR Profile table.

questions.stem: If the HRSD application is scoped, why can the System Administrator initially access all HR applications after the plugin has been installed?

options.text: When the HR plugins are installed, the necessary HR roles are added to the Admin role.
The roles were manually granted by a ServiceNow security user.
The Admin will always have access to all HR tables and data.
The roles were manually granted by an HR Admin.

questions.explanation: When HR plugins are installed, the necessary HR roles (including sn_hr_core.admin) are automatically added to the Admin role. This gives System Administrators initial access to all HR applications for setup and configuration. After implementation, the HR Admin role should be removed from the Admin role to protect confidential HR data.

questions.stem:
Scenario: You have an existing ITSM customer who is now implementing HR Enterprise. In UAT, they discovered that they get an error message about a Read operation from the HR scope to the Global scope being denied. You have verified that each Script Include was written correctly.
What else must be done to allow the Script Includes to work in the HR application?

options.text: The Status of the associated record on the Application Restricted Caller Access list must be set to Denied.
You must create a custom ACL to allow the script includes to work.
The Status of the associated record on the Application Restricted Caller Access list must be set to Allowed.
You must change Scope for the script includes to work.

questions.explanation: When a cross-scope script include call is denied, the status on the Application Restricted Caller Access list must be set to Allowed. The Restricted Caller Access framework tracks and controls cross-scope API calls in scoped applications. Setting the status to Allowed permits the HR scope to call script includes in the Global scope.

questions.stem: In the HR Guided Setup Module, the Configuration View displays which of the following for a Category? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: In the HR Guided Setup Module, the Configuration View for a Category displays Properties (A), Lists (D), and Forms (F). Properties allow setting system properties, Lists display configurable list views, and Forms provide form configuration options. Gauges (B), Dashboards (C), and Overviews (E) are not part of the Configuration View in Guided Setup.

questions.stem: What method needs to be invoked from MatchingRuleProcessor class?
questions.explanation: The processAndGetCandidates method from the MatchingRuleProcessor class is invoked to process matching rules and retrieve a list of candidate agents for HR case assignment. This method evaluates the matching criteria against available agents and returns the set of candidates that meet the defined conditions.

questions.stem: If an HR Service will only be used internally by HR professionals, what is the minimum configuration needed?

options.text: HR Service, HR Template, and Record Producer.
HR Service, HR Template, Record Producer, and Lifecycle event type.

questions.explanation: If an HR Service will only be used internally by HR professionals (not exposed to employees via the portal), the minimum configuration needed is just the HR Service record itself. No HR Template is needed because internal agents can fill in fields manually, and no Record Producer is needed since employees won't be submitting requests for this service.

questions.stem: The Knowledge bases searched for the Knowledge results section on an HR Case are determined by what?
questions.explanation: The Knowledge Bases searched in the Knowledge results section on an HR Case are determined by the Contextual Search configuration. Contextual Search defines which knowledge bases are queried when showing suggested articles on a case form. This is configured under Contextual Search > Search Contexts and allows administrators to specify which KBs are relevant for HR cases.

questions.stem:
When gathering requirements for HR Services, it is best to begin by defining the Service then working upwards, categorizing in progressively more detail.
What are the basic categories used?

options.text: HR Service, Topic Category, Activity Category, Activities, COE.
HR Service, Topic Detail, Topic Category, COE.

questions.explanation: The basic HR Service categorization hierarchy from most specific to broadest is: HR Service (the individual service), Topic Detail (specific service grouping), Topic Category (broader grouping), and COE (Center of Excellence, the broadest HR departmental category). You start by defining the service then work upward categorizing in progressively more detail (broader categories).

questions.stem: If a knowledge base and its articles have no user criteria selected, a user without a role can do what?

options.text: can neither read nor contribute articles

questions.explanation: If a Knowledge Base and its articles have no User Criteria selected, a user without a role can read articles but not contribute. When no Can Read criteria is set, the KB is open for reading by all users. However, contributing (creating/editing articles) still requires appropriate permissions, which a user without any role would not have by default.

questions.stem: How does ServiceNow know which HR Template to use on an HR Case?

options.text: The HR Template is referenced on the HR Service record.
The HR Template is referenced on the record producer form.
Each COE has a specific HR Template.
The HR Template is selected directly on the Catalog item.

questions.explanation: ServiceNow knows which HR Template to use on an HR Case because the HR Template is referenced directly on the HR Service record. The Template field on the HR Service links to a specific HR Template, so when a case is created for that service, the system automatically applies the associated template to populate case fields.

questions.stem: What are the key differentiators between an HR Profile record and a User record? (Choose three.)

options.text: The HR Profile stores the employee's assigned delegates.
The HR Profile includes group membership information.
The HR Profile includes employee organizational information like Colleagues.
The HR Profile stores login credential information.
The HR Profile may include employee marital status.
The HR Profile is intended to store confidential employee data that is pertinent for HR.

questions.explanation: Key differentiators between HR Profile and User record: HR Profile includes employee organizational info like Colleagues (C), may include marital status (E), and is intended for confidential employee data pertinent to HR (F). The User record stores login credentials (D) and group membership (B), not the HR Profile. Delegates (A) are stored on the User record, not the HR Profile.

questions.stem: If a customer has a huge employee population, complex organizational structures, and requires custom integrations and language translations, what level of configuration complexity would their project be considered?
questions.explanation: A customer with a huge employee population, complex organizational structures, and requirements for custom integrations and language translations would be classified as Drastic configuration complexity. ServiceNow's implementation methodology classifies projects by complexity levels, and Drastic represents the highest level requiring the most effort, customization, and extended timelines.

questions.stem: When an employee completes a questionnaire on an Employee Form, on which table does the system store their answers?
questions.explanation: When an employee completes a questionnaire on an Employee Form, the system stores their answers in the Metric Result [asmt_metric_result] table. ServiceNow uses the Assessment framework for surveys and questionnaires, where individual responses are recorded as metric results. The asmt_metric_result table captures the score, value, and details for each question answered.

questions.stem: With the I18N: Knowledge Management Internationalization Plugin v2 enabled, how are translated Knowledge articles associated with each other so that the user is presented with the article in the selected language?
questions.explanation: With the I18N Knowledge Management Internationalization Plugin v2, translated Knowledge articles are associated through the Translated Versions related list. This list links the original article to its translations in different languages, allowing the system to display the correct language version based on the user's selected language preference.

questions.stem: When creating a PDF Document Template, where does the list of Document Revisions come from?
questions.explanation: When creating a PDF Document Template, the list of Document Revisions comes from Managed Documents. The Document Revision field references revisions of Managed Document records, which are versioned documents stored in the document management system. The HR admin selects the appropriate revision of a managed document to use as the PDF template.

questions.stem: Only users with which role, at a minimum, may view the confidential data on the HR Profiles table?
questions.explanation: The Profile Reader [sn_hr_core.profile_reader] role is the minimum required to view confidential data on the HR Profiles table. This role provides read-only access to confidential HR profile fields. Profile Writer (A) provides write access, and the HR Case roles (C, D) are for lifecycle events case access, not profile data viewing.

questions.stem: What determines if a user can view a Knowledge article?
questions.explanation: The Can/Cannot Read User Criteria determines if a user can view a Knowledge article. User Criteria with Can Read defines who has read access, and Cannot Read defines explicit denials. Can/Cannot Contribute (B) controls article editing, not viewing. HR Criteria (C) is for HR-specific content, and ACL Rules (D) are the underlying mechanism but User Criteria is the configured method.

questions.stem: What do Client Roles define?

options.text: Roles that come into force if user uses a browser client.
Named roles (eg VP of Operations, SVP Sales) for a customer’s clients.
Access for new hires, employees, alumni, contingent, and contract workers.

questions.explanation: Client Roles define access for different employee types such as new hires, employees, alumni, contingent workers, and contract workers. They are automatically assigned based on the employment type on the HR Profile and determine what an employee can see and do on the Employee Service Center. They are not browser-based roles or named executive roles.

questions.stem: When a Guided Setup task is marked as complete, how can it be reopened?

options.text: Click the Mark as Incomplete button

questions.explanation: When a Guided Setup task is marked as complete, it can be reopened by clicking the Mark as Incomplete button. This allows administrators to revisit and modify previously completed configuration tasks without restarting the entire Guided Setup. The button appears on completed tasks in the Guided Setup interface.

questions.stem:
When creating a PDF Document template, the Document revision field must be completed.
How does the system determine which documents are available to be selected for this field?

options.text: You must be a member of the Owning Group for the Managed Document
Your group memberships and the Document owner field on the Managed Document record
You must have created the Managed Document record

questions.explanation: The system determines which documents are available for the Document Revision field based on your group memberships and the Document Owner field on the Managed Document record. Only Managed Documents where the current user's groups match the ownership criteria are visible for selection, ensuring proper access control over document templates.

questions.stem: What is used to create a link on an HR Case form that accesses information outside the application?
questions.explanation: The Link Generator is used to create links on an HR Case form that access information outside the application. It generates buttons or links that can navigate to external systems, web pages, or other ServiceNow applications. The Link Generator handles URL construction and script-based link generation for cross-application access from HR cases.

questions.stem: When configuring a PDF Document Template, how does the system map form fields to ServiceNow fields?

options.text: The Document field type on the PDF Template Mappings record
The Preview value field on the PDF Template Mappings record
The Mapping field on the PDF Template Mappings record
The Document field on the PDF Template Mappings record

questions.explanation: When configuring a PDF Document Template, the Mapping field on the PDF Template Mappings record maps form fields to ServiceNow fields. The Mapping field defines the dot-walk relationship between the PDF form field and the corresponding ServiceNow record field, enabling dynamic population of PDF documents with case or profile data.

questions.stem: If the Match All field is checked on a User Criteria record, the user:

options.text: Must satisfy at least one of the criteria to meet the conditions.
Must satisfy at least of the criteria to meet the conditions.
Must satisfy a majority percentage of the criteria to meet the conditions.
Must satisfy all of the selected criteria to meet the conditions.

questions.explanation: When the Match All field is checked on a User Criteria record, the user must satisfy all of the selected criteria to meet the conditions. This applies AND logic across all criteria fields (company, department, group, location, etc.). Without Match All checked, the user only needs to satisfy at least one criterion (OR logic).

questions.stem: If a new HR Knowledge base is created, how can it be included in the Knowledge results section on the HR Case form?

options.text: Add it to the HR Template
Add it to the HR Service configuration
All Knowledge bases are searched by default
Add it to the Contextual Search configuration

questions.explanation: To include a new HR Knowledge Base in the Knowledge results section on the HR Case form, you must add it to the Contextual Search configuration. Contextual Search defines which knowledge bases the system queries when displaying suggested articles. Navigate to Contextual Search configuration and add the new KB to the search context used by HR cases.

questions.stem: How is the HR template associated with an HR service?

options.text: On the Lifecycle Event Activity Set

questions.explanation: The HR Template is associated with an HR Service on the HR Service record itself. The Template field on the HR Service record links to the specific HR Template that will auto-populate fields when a case is created for that service. This association is configured directly on the service, not on the template or other records.

questions.stem: Where does the HR Administrator define which HR Profile fields can be edited in the ServiceNow instance?
questions.explanation: The HR Administrator defines which HR Profile fields can be edited in the ServiceNow instance through HR Administration > Properties. This module contains system properties that control HR Profile field editability, including which fields are visible, required, or read-only. It centralizes HR application configuration settings.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the Owning Group field on the HR Template?

options.text: They approve the Template to be published.
They manage updates to the Template.
HR Cases are assigned to the Owning Group.

questions.explanation: The Owning Group field on the HR Template identifies the group that manages updates to the Template. The owning group is responsible for maintaining and modifying the template configuration over time. They do not approve publication (A) or own the lifecycle event (B), and HR Cases are assigned based on assignment groups, not the template's owning group (D).

questions.stem:
The Enterprise Service Management Integrations framework contains common components to be used for integrating HR applications with third-party systems.
Which capability does the Enterprise Service Management Integrations framework leverage to communicate with external instances and third-party systems?
questions.explanation: The Enterprise Service Management Integrations framework leverages Flow Designer to communicate with external instances and third-party systems. Flow Designer provides the automation engine with built-in actions, spokes, and integration capabilities to orchestrate data exchange between ServiceNow HRSD and external HR systems without custom coding.

questions.stem: What are some of the benefits of having separate COE tables? (Choose two.)

options.text: Allows for an extra layer of security within the HR organization.
Allows HR case agents to gather the right information based on the Service.
Eliminates the need for an HR case agent.
Eliminates the need to create database views.

questions.explanation: Separate COE (Center of Excellence) tables provide two key benefits: an extra layer of security within the HR organization (A) by isolating data per COE (e.g., payroll data separate from employee relations), and allowing HR case agents to gather the right information based on the Service (B) by presenting COE-specific fields and forms tailored to each service type.

questions.stem: Who can generate the PDF document on an active HR Case?
questions.explanation: Only the Assigned to person on the HR Case can generate the PDF document from an active case. This restricts document generation to the agent who is responsible for the case, ensuring proper accountability. The subject person's manager, HR managers, and employees cannot generate the document unless they are the assigned agent.

questions.stem: What role is required to access the modules in the HR Integrations application?
questions.explanation: The HR Integrations Admin [sn_hr_integrations.admin] role is required to access the modules in the HR Integrations application. This scoped admin role provides full access to configure integration sources, schema mappings, and web services within the HR Integrations application scope. It is separate from the core HR Admin or system Admin roles.

questions.stem:
In the base ServiceNow platform, the Human Resources General Knowledge base has Can Contribute User Criteria set to Users with the [sn_hr_core.kb_write] role.
If a Knowledge article in the Human Resources General Knowledge base has no Can Contribute User Criteria set, what is the minimum role a user would need to edit the article?
questions.explanation: Since the Knowledge Base has Can Contribute User Criteria set to users with sn_hr_core.kb_write, and the article has no article-level Can Contribute criteria, the KB-level criteria applies. A user needs the KB Writer [sn_hr_core.kb_writer] role (which includes kb_write) to contribute to articles. When no article-level criteria exists, the KB-level criteria is inherited.

questions.stem: In which module can the HR admin manage the HR email address for incoming HR requests?
questions.explanation: The HR admin manages the HR email address for incoming HR requests through HR Administration > Properties. This module contains the property that defines the inbound email address used by the HR application. System Properties > Email Properties and Email Setup are platform-level modules, not HR-specific configuration.

questions.stem: In the base ServiceNow configuration, when are HR Cases created after a Bulk HR case request is submitted?

options.text: Twice per day using a scheduled job
Every 6 hours using a scheduled job
Once a day using a scheduled job

questions.explanation: In the base ServiceNow configuration, HR Cases are created immediately after a Bulk HR Case request is submitted. Unlike some bulk operations that use scheduled jobs, bulk case creation processes the request synchronously and generates individual HR Cases for each matching employee right away upon submission.

questions.stem:
An employee in Chicago submits a request using the Employee Service Center. The HR Case template associated with the HR Service defines the Skills needed, but not an Assignment Group.
Using base platform functionality, which of the following is the first step the system takes to assign the Case?

options.text: An Assignment Rule creates a list of possible assignees
A Matching Rule assigns the Case to a group
The Case must be manually assigned
An Assignment Rule assigns the Case to a group

questions.explanation: When the HR Template defines skills but no Assignment Group, the system first uses an Assignment Rule to assign the Case to a group. Assignment Rules evaluate case conditions (including location, COE) to determine the appropriate assignment group. Matching Rules (B) match agents within a group but don't assign to groups. The assignment rule is the first step in the assignment process.

questions.stem: Which of the following are predefined Dashboards that are installed with HR Case Management? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The predefined dashboards installed with HR Case Management are: Manager Dashboard (A) for manager oversight of team cases, Overview (B) for a summary view of all HR operations, and HR Case Dashboard (F) for detailed case metrics. Workforce Administration, Onboarding, and Employee Relations dashboards are either separate products or not included in base HR Case Management.

questions.stem:
ServiceNow has identified 3 maturity levels for an HR customer.
What are they?
questions.explanation: ServiceNow identifies three HR maturity levels: Managed Interactions (basic case management and tracking), Self-Reliance (employee self-service through portals and knowledge bases), and Smart Services (AI-driven automation and predictive capabilities). These represent the progression from reactive HR support to proactive, intelligent service delivery.

questions.stem: When using the Generate HR Profiles module to create HR Profiles, what field must be completed to ensure the employees are granted the appropriate Client Role?
questions.explanation: When using the Generate HR Profiles module, the Employment type field must be completed to ensure employees are granted the appropriate Client Role. Client Roles are automatically assigned based on the employment type (e.g., full-time employee, contractor, contingent worker), which determines what access and content the employee receives on the Employee Service Center.

questions.stem: What does the employee utilize when submitting a self-service request to the HR Organization?
questions.explanation: Employees use the HR Catalog when submitting self-service requests to the HR Organization. The HR Catalog contains Record Producers and catalog items that employees can browse on the Employee Service Center to request HR services. The catalog provides a structured way for employees to find and request specific HR services.

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of HR Topic Categories?

options.text: They group common HR Catalog Items.

questions.explanation: HR Topic Categories group common HR Services together for organizational purposes. They provide a logical grouping structure in the HR service catalog hierarchy: COE > Topic Category > Topic Detail > HR Service. Topic Categories help employees find related services and help administrators organize the HR service portfolio.

questions.stem: What are the benefits of the HR application being scoped? (Choose three.)

options.text: Provides an additional layer of control over HR data.
Allows HR Admins to configure the HR application.
HR department has more autonomy to manage all aspects of HRSD.
Allows the System Administrator complete control.
HR department has full control of the global application.

questions.explanation: The benefits of HRSD being a scoped application are: it provides an additional layer of control over HR data (A) through application scope isolation, allows HR Admins to configure the HR application (B) independently within the scope, and gives the HR department more autonomy to manage all aspects of HRSD (C). System Admin having complete control (D) is actually what scoping prevents, and HR does not control the global application (E).

questions.stem:
The HR Admin [sn_hr_core.admin] role allows the user to add members to groups.
What additional role is needed for an HR Admin to remove users from groups?
questions.explanation: The User Admin [user_admin] role is needed in addition to HR Admin to remove users from groups. The HR Admin role allows adding members to groups, but removing group membership requires the user_admin role which provides broader user record management capabilities. User Writer (B) and User Reader (C) don't provide group management, and HR User Admin (D) doesn't exist as a standard role.

questions.stem:
On the HR Case form, some HR Services have associated Response templates.
What determines which HR Services have Response Templates?

options.text: The HR Criteria on the HR Service
The HR Criteria on the Response Template record
The table and conditions on the Response Template record
The User Criteria on the HR Service

questions.explanation: Which HR Services have Response Templates is determined by the table and conditions on the Response Template record itself. Response Templates specify which table they apply to and filter conditions that control when they appear. The template's conditions determine which HR Cases show the response template option, based on case attributes like COE or service type.

questions.stem: At what level is User Criteria set to control who can read and edit knowledge articles?

options.text: In either the Knowledge Base or Article.

questions.explanation: User Criteria can be set at either the Knowledge Base level or the Article level to control who can read and edit articles. KB-level criteria provides a baseline for all articles in the base, while article-level criteria can further restrict or expand access for individual articles. Both levels work together to provide granular access control.

questions.stem: How many COEs may be associated with an HR Service?
questions.explanation: Only one COE (Center of Excellence) may be associated with an HR Service. Each HR Service belongs to exactly one COE, which determines the COE-specific table where cases are stored and the security boundaries that apply. This one-to-one relationship ensures clear data isolation and proper routing of HR cases to the right department.

questions.stem: Which module provides a user-friendly interface for creating new HR Skills and assigning HR skills to members of the HR department?
questions.explanation: The Manage HR Skills module provides a user-friendly interface for creating new HR Skills and assigning HR skills to members of the HR department. It allows administrators to define skill categories, create individual skills, and associate them with HR agents for matching rule-based case assignment.

questions.stem: Which table is considered the core table for all HR Case records?
questions.explanation: The HR Case [sn_hr_core_case] table is the core table for all HR Case records. It extends the Task table and serves as the parent table for all COE-specific case tables (Employee Relations, Payroll, etc.). All HR case data ultimately rolls up to sn_hr_core_case, making it the central table for HR case management.

questions.stem: Which HR Role is typically granted to all HR Support staff, at a minimum?
questions.explanation: The HR Basic [sn_hr_core.basic] role is typically granted to all HR Support staff at a minimum. It provides the foundational permissions needed to work with HR cases, view HR profiles, and access basic HR functionality. HR Admin (A) is for administrators, KB Writer (C) is for knowledge authors, and Document Management User (D) is for document management.

questions.stem: A user with only the HR Admin [sn_hr_core.admin] role can save and modify which copies of existing reports?
questions.explanation: A user with only the HR Admin [sn_hr_core.admin] role can save and modify Personal copies of existing reports. Without the report_admin or admin role, users can only create and modify their own personal reports. Global (B) and Group (C) report modifications require elevated report administration roles. All (A) is only available to report administrators.

questions.stem: What is the difference between a configuration and a customization?

options.text: Configuration uses complex JavaScript while Customization involves field name changes and new buttons.
There is no difference between Configuration and Customization.
Customization uses the built-in tools in the platform while Configuration involves code changes.
Configuration uses the built-in tools in the platform while Customization involves code changes.

questions.explanation: Configuration uses the built-in tools in the platform (form designer, list layout, system properties, etc.) while Customization involves code changes (scripts, business rules, script includes). Configuration is preferred because it uses supported platform features that are upgrade-safe, while customization requires development effort and may need maintenance during upgrades.

questions.stem: Which Service Portal configuration option is used to customize the logo, theme, and title of the HR Service Portal?
questions.explanation: The Branding Editor is the Service Portal configuration option used to customize the logo, theme, and title of the HR Service Portal. It provides a visual interface for modifying the portal's appearance including colors, logos, fonts, and other branding elements without requiring code changes. Designer (A) is for page layout, Page Editor (B) is for content, and Widget Editor (C) is for widget code.

questions.stem: What is the minimum role required to access the HR Properties module?
questions.explanation: The HR Admin [sn_hr_core.admin] role is the minimum required to access the HR Properties module. HR Administration > Properties contains HR-specific system settings, and the HR Admin role provides the necessary permissions to view and modify these properties. Admin (C) also has access but is not the minimum HR-specific role.

questions.stem: The HR Case [sn_hr_core_case] table is an extension of what?
questions.explanation: The HR Case [sn_hr_core_case] table extends the Task [task] table. This inheritance gives HR Cases all the standard task functionality (assignment, state management, SLAs, approvals, work notes) while adding HR-specific fields. It is not an extension of Incident, Case, or Lifecycle Events tables.

questions.stem: What role is required to assign scoped HR roles?
questions.explanation: The HR Admin [sn_hr_core.admin] role is required to assign scoped HR roles. Since HRSD is a scoped application, assigning roles within the HR scope requires the HR Admin role or higher. HR Manager (B) and HR Basic (D) do not have permissions to assign roles, and LE Admin (C) is specific to lifecycle events, not role management.

questions.stem:
The customer you are implementing has purchased HR Service Delivery Enterprise which includes Enterprise Onboarding and Transitions.
Which plugin must be activated to utilize Enterprise Onboarding and Transitions?

options.text: Human Resources Scoped App: Lifecycle Events [com.sn_hr_lifecycle_events]

questions.explanation: The Human Resources Scoped App: Lifecycle Events [com.sn_hr_lifecycle_events] plugin must be activated to utilize Enterprise Onboarding and Transitions. This plugin provides the lifecycle events framework including activity sets, trigger conditions, and the onboarding/offboarding process automation that Enterprise Onboarding requires.

questions.stem: The Lifecycle Events [sn_hr_le_case] table is a direct extension of which table?
questions.explanation: The Lifecycle Events [sn_hr_le_case] table is a direct extension of the HR Case [sn_hr_core_case] table. This means lifecycle event cases inherit all HR Case functionality while adding lifecycle-specific fields like activity sets and trigger conditions. It does not directly extend Task or COE-specific tables.

questions.stem: Delegated Developers are granted access only to what in which they are working?
questions.explanation: Delegated Developers are granted access only to the Scopes in which they are working. The delegated_developer role provides development capabilities (creating scripts, business rules, etc.) within a specific application scope without granting system admin access. This scoped access follows ServiceNow's application isolation model.

questions.stem:
The customer you will be implementing for wants to utilize Now Mobile.
What is the minimum HR SKU they may purchase that includes Now Mobile?

options.text: Now Mobile is a standalone solution

questions.explanation: HR Service Delivery Professional is the minimum HR SKU that includes Now Mobile. The Professional tier adds mobile access, Advanced Work Assignment, and other features beyond what the Standard tier provides. Enterprise includes everything in Professional plus additional capabilities like Lifecycle Events Enterprise. Now Mobile is not a standalone solution for HRSD.

questions.stem: If the HR Admin [sn_hr_core.admin] needs to develop within the HR application but cannot have the system Admin role, what additional role should be granted?
questions.explanation: The Delegated Developer [delegated_developer] role should be granted to an HR Admin who needs to develop within the HR application but cannot have the system Admin role. This role provides development capabilities (script editing, business rule creation) within the HR application scope without the full system administration privileges.

questions.stem:
When a Document Template is created from an HR Case, the name of the person who created the document is added to the name of the attachment.
Why?

options.text: It indicates who should sign the document
It indicates who generated the document
It indicates the Opened for user
It indicates who the document is about

questions.explanation: When a Document Template creates a document from an HR Case, the name of the person who created the document is added to the attachment name to indicate who generated the document. This provides an audit trail showing which HR professional created the document, which is important for accountability and compliance tracking.

questions.stem: How can fields for a specific HR Service be displayed on the New Case Creation page?

options.text: HR Service-specific fields cannot be added to the New Case Creation page
Using the Case Creation Service Configurations
Using the Case Options field on the HR Service

questions.explanation: Fields for a specific HR Service can be displayed on the New Case Creation page using Case Creation Service Configurations. This feature allows administrators to define service-specific fields that appear during case creation, ensuring agents capture the right information for each HR service type without cluttering the form with irrelevant fields.

questions.stem: Which field on the HR Service record defines which HR Catalog Item is associated with the Service?
questions.explanation: The Record Producer field on the HR Service record defines which HR Catalog Item is associated with the service. The Record Producer is the catalog item that employees use to submit requests on the Employee Service Center. It creates the user-facing form and generates the HR Case when submitted.

questions.stem: What must be updated or loaded into the Customer's instance before importing the stories?
questions.explanation: Products must be updated or loaded into the customer's instance before importing stories. In ServiceNow Agile Development, stories are associated with Products, so the Product records must exist first to establish the proper relationships when stories are imported. Without Products, the stories cannot be properly categorized.

questions.stem: When the Lifecycle Events application is installed, the LE Admin role is granted to which role?

options.text: It is not added to other roles

questions.explanation: When the Lifecycle Events application is installed, the LE Admin [sn_hr_le.admin] role is automatically granted to the HR Admin [sn_hr_core.admin] role. This gives existing HR Administrators immediate access to configure lifecycle events without requiring manual role assignment. The LE Admin role inherits through the HR Admin role hierarchy.

questions.stem: Which of the following applications is installed with the Human Resources Scoped App: Core plugin?
questions.explanation: HR Case Management is installed with the Human Resources Scoped App: Core [com.sn_hr_core] plugin. The Core plugin provides the foundational HR functionality including case management, HR profiles, HR services, and the case assignment framework. Employee Service Center (A), Document Management (B), and Lifecycle Events (C) are separate plugins.

questions.stem: If you wanted someone to administer the Employee Service Center without granting them the HR Admin role, which scoped Admin role would they need?
questions.explanation: The Service Portal Admin [sn_hr_sp.admin] role allows someone to administer the Employee Service Center without the HR Admin role. This scoped role provides configuration access specifically for the Employee Service Center portal, including page layout, widget configuration, and portal branding, without granting broader HR administration capabilities.

questions.stem: When does the platform assign a Client Role to a user?

options.text: Client Roles must be manually added to each employee record
When an HR Profile is created or modified for the employee
Client Roles are automatically added with Group membership
When a User record is created for the employee

questions.explanation: The platform assigns a Client Role to a user when an HR Profile is created or modified for the employee. Client Roles are automatically determined based on the employment type field on the HR Profile. When a profile is generated or updated, the system evaluates the employment type and assigns the corresponding client role (e.g., employee, contractor, alumni).

questions.stem: If you had little coding experience and were tasked with adding new pages to the customer’s Employee Service Center, which Service Portal Configuration option would be best to complete the task?
questions.explanation: The Service Portal Designer provides a drag-and-drop graphical interface for adding and arranging pages without requiring coding experience. It allows adding new pages, placing widgets, and configuring layouts visually. Page Editor (A) requires more technical knowledge, Widget Editor (C) requires JavaScript/Angular skills, and Branding Editor (D) is only for visual styling.

questions.stem: What provides a graphical interface to create survey categories, questions, configure the details, and publish the survey?
questions.explanation: The Survey Designer provides a graphical interface to create survey categories, configure question details, and publish surveys. It offers a visual drag-and-drop experience for building assessments with different question types (rating scale, text, choice) and organizing them into categories. It is the primary tool for survey creation in ServiceNow.

questions.stem: HR Administrators can configure a personal copy of the HR Case Dashboard using which of the following buttons? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: HR Administrators can configure a personal copy of the HR Case Dashboard using the Change Layout (A) button to modify the dashboard layout and the Add Content (D) button to add new widgets and reports. These are standard ServiceNow dashboard customization options. Delete Content (B) and Modify Layout (C) are not separate buttons, and Add Layout (E) does not exist.

questions.stem: What determines when the HR Chat queue is available?

options.text: Schedule field on the HR Profile
Schedule field on the User record
Schedule field on the Queues record

questions.explanation: The HR Chat queue availability is determined by the Schedule field on the Queues record. The Queue configuration includes a schedule that defines when agents are available to receive chat requests. Outside of the scheduled hours, the chat queue is not available to employees. This is configured per queue, not per user or profile.

questions.stem: What defines the path the Case or HR Task will take when it is escalated?
questions.explanation: Escalation Rules define the path a Case or HR Task will take when it is escalated. They specify the conditions that trigger escalation (such as time elapsed without action) and the actions to take (reassign, notify, change priority). Assignment Rules handle initial assignment, Business Rules handle data logic, and Matching Rules match agents to cases.

questions.stem: If the HR Administrator group has been tasked with collecting Performance Analytics data, what additional role should be granted to the group?
questions.explanation: The Performance Analytics Data Collector [pa_data_collector] role should be granted for collecting PA data. This role allows running data collection jobs that gather metrics and indicator data. PA Administrator (B) provides too much access, Threshold Admin (C) is only for threshold configuration, and System Administrator (D) is excessive for this task.

questions.stem: If the HR Administrator has only been given the HR Admin [sn_hr_core.admin] role, what additional role is necessary for them to configure all aspects of the Employee Document Management application?
questions.explanation: The EF Admin [sn_hr_ef.admin] role is needed to configure all aspects of the Employee Document Management application. The HR Admin role alone does not include Employee Document Management administration permissions because it is a separate scoped application. The EF Admin role provides full configuration access to document types, retention policies, and legal holds.

questions.stem: If both the Knowledge Base and the KB article have no "Can Read" User Criteria, what role is required to read the article?
questions.explanation: If both the Knowledge Base and the KB article have no Can Read User Criteria set, no role is needed to read the article. When no User Criteria restrictions are configured at either level, the knowledge base is effectively open for public reading. Any authenticated user can access the articles regardless of their roles.

questions.stem: Using the base HRSD configuration with no integrations, when the subject person electronically signs an HR document or PDF document, the signature is saved as what?

options.text: a picture of the signature that is added to the document

questions.explanation: In the base HRSD configuration without integrations, when an employee electronically signs an HR document, the signature is saved as a picture of the signature added to the document. The base platform captures the signature as an image (drawn or typed) and embeds it in the document. Digital signatures (A), digital keys (C), and digital certificates (D) require additional integration with signing providers.

questions.stem: What role needs to be removed from the Admin role at go live to prevent the System Admin from being able to see HR Profile information?
questions.explanation: The HR Admin [sn_hr_core.admin] role needs to be removed from the Admin role at go-live to prevent the System Admin from seeing HR Profile information. When HR plugins are installed, HR Admin is added to Admin by default for initial setup. Removing it at go-live ensures only users with explicit HR roles can access confidential employee data.

questions.stem:
If you select Data Type Numeric Scale on the Assessment Metric (Survey Question) form there is a Scale definition field made visible.
What does it mean to select High for the Scale definition?

options.text: It means a high score is bad
It means a high score is good
There is no option for Scale definition
There is no option for High

questions.explanation: When selecting High for the Scale definition on a Numeric Scale assessment question, it means a high score is good. The Scale definition indicates the direction of the scale — High means higher values are positive/desirable. This is used for scoring calculations and analytics to properly interpret whether high or low scores indicate favorable responses.

questions.stem: In which Application Scope is the Lifecycle Events table contained?
questions.explanation: The Lifecycle Events table is contained in the Human Resources: Lifecycle Events application scope [com.sn_hr_lifecycle_events]. This scoped application provides the lifecycle event framework separately from Core HR. The table sn_hr_le_case and related lifecycle event tables belong to this scope, not Core (A), Integrations (C), or Service Portal (D).

questions.stem: What settings define and track cross-scope access to applications?
questions.explanation: Restricted Caller Access defines and tracks cross-scope access to applications. In ServiceNow's scoped application model, when one scope attempts to call an API in another scope, the Restricted Caller Access framework logs the attempt and can allow, deny, or track it. This is the mechanism that controls cross-scope communication in HRSD.

questions.stem: What determines which Knowledge bases, Knowledge articles, and Service Catalog Items an employee can view?
questions.explanation: User Criteria determines which Knowledge Bases, Knowledge articles, and Service Catalog Items an employee can view. User Criteria is the platform-level mechanism for controlling access to these resources based on user attributes (roles, groups, departments, etc.). HR Criteria controls HR-specific content on the Employee Service Center, not KBs and catalog items.

questions.stem: The Template field referenced on the HR Service record is used to do what?

options.text: Populate fields on the HR Case record
Filter who can access the HR Service
Create pre-configured responses HR professionals can use
Make the HR Service accessible on the Employee Service Center

questions.explanation: The Template field on the HR Service record is used to populate fields on the HR Case record. When a case is created for that HR Service, the linked HR Template auto-fills case fields like assignment group, skills, priority, and other attributes. This streamlines case creation and ensures consistent data entry across similar requests.

questions.stem: When is the Record producer field needed on the HR Service record?

options.text: When the HR professional will be creating Cases on behalf of the employee
When you want the employee to request the HR Service from the Employee Service Center
It is always a required field
There is no Record producer held on the HR Service record

questions.explanation: The Record Producer field is needed on the HR Service record when you want the employee to request the HR Service from the Employee Service Center. The Record Producer creates the user-facing catalog item that employees interact with. Without it, the service is only available for internal HR professional use and cannot be self-served by employees.

questions.stem: What are the major HR Service Catalog components? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The major HR Service Catalog components are: HR Template (A) for auto-populating case fields, HR Catalog Item (C) as the browsable catalog entry, Record Producer (E) for the employee-facing request form, and HR Service (F) as the core service definition. Assignment Group (B), Matching Rule (D), and HR Profile (G) are related but not primary catalog components.

questions.stem: How can HR Tasks be marked as optional?

options.text: Set Optional to True on the HR Task Template
Set Optional to True on the Activity Set
Set Optional to True on the HR Case form

questions.explanation: HR Tasks can be marked as optional by setting Optional to True on the HR Task Template. This configuration on the task template level means that when the task is generated from the template, it will be flagged as optional and can be skipped without blocking case closure. Activity Sets (B) and the HR Case form (D) don't have this option.

questions.stem: What provides a graphical representation of other tables related to a specific table, either through class extension or reference?
questions.explanation: The Schema Map provides a graphical representation of tables related to a specific table, showing class extensions and reference relationships. It visually displays the table hierarchy and field references, making it easy to understand data model relationships. Access it by navigating to System Definition > Tables and clicking Schema Map.

questions.stem:
Scenario: An existing ITSM customer is now implementing HR Enterprise. As part of the implementation, the Scoped Application Restricted Caller Access [com.glide.scope.access.restricted_caller] plugin was automatically activated.
By default, what is the Caller Access field set to?
questions.explanation: By default, the Caller Access field on the Scoped Application Restricted Caller Access plugin is set to Caller Restriction. This means cross-scope calls are tracked and restricted by default, requiring explicit approval before one application scope can call APIs in another scope. This default ensures security between application scopes.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the key factor in determining the implementation timeline?
questions.explanation: Configuration complexity is the key factor in determining the implementation timeline. Factors like the number of employees, organizational structure complexity, number of integrations, language requirements, and customization needs all contribute to configuration complexity, which directly impacts how long the implementation will take.

questions.stem: Beginning with the Orlando release, which module allows HR Administrators to define which groups may access the various COEs or HR Services without needing to edit or create new ACL records?
questions.explanation: Beginning with Orlando, the COE ACL Configuration module allows HR Administrators to define which groups may access various COEs or HR Services without creating ACL records. This provides a code-free way to manage COE-level access control through a simple configuration interface rather than requiring technical ACL expertise.

questions.stem:
Scenario: You have an existing ITSM customer who is now implementing HR Enterprise. In UAT, they discovered that a new button on the HR case, created using the Link Generator application, is not displaying the appropriate web page. Instead, they get a Page Not Found error. You have verified that the Link configuration and script are both accurate.
What else must be done to allow the Link to work?

options.text: The Status of the associated record on the Application Restricted Caller Access list must be set to Denied.
You must create a custom ACL to allow the link to work.
The Status of the associated record on the Application Restricted Caller Access list must be set to Allowed.
You must change Scope for the link to work.

questions.explanation: The Status of the associated record on the Application Restricted Caller Access list must be set to Allowed. When a Link Generator button gets a Page Not Found error despite correct configuration, it's because the cross-scope call from the HR scope to the target scope is being blocked. Setting the Restricted Caller Access status to Allowed permits the cross-scope access.

questions.stem:
A customer using Lifecycle Events Enterprise has documented a large offboarding Lifecycle Event that includes many steps. Many of the steps, including approvals, must be completed in a specific order.
Which of these is the best method to use to ensure the activities are triggered in the appropriate order?

options.text: Create a new lifecycle event for each of the dependent items
Create separate trigger conditions for each of the dependent activities
Create activity containers for the dependent items
Create separate activity sets for each of the dependent activities

questions.explanation: Activity containers are the best method to ensure lifecycle event activities are triggered in the appropriate order with dependencies. Activity containers manage dependencies and sequencing within an activity set, ensuring that child activities execute in the correct order with proper predecessor-successor relationships. They handle approval chains and sequential step execution.

questions.stem: What kinds of records can be created using HR Service Activities? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: HR Service Activities can create Approvals (B) and Tasks (D). Activities within an HR Service can generate approval requests that must be completed before proceeding, and tasks that are assigned to agents or employees for completion. Workflows (A) and HR Templates (C) are configuration elements, not records created by service activities.

questions.stem: Which HR Integrations module is used to document the URL, basic integration properties, and inbound and outbound username and password information for a third-party application?
questions.explanation: The Sources module in HR Integrations documents the URL, basic integration properties, and inbound/outbound username and password information for third-party applications. Each source record represents a connection endpoint to an external system, centralizing the connection details needed for data exchange between ServiceNow HRSD and third-party HR systems.

questions.stem: How can a PDF document on an active HR case be generated? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: A PDF document on an active HR Case can be generated two ways: autogenerated by system configuration (A) when the HR Service has case options configured for automatic document generation, or by the Assigned to person (D) who can manually trigger document generation from the case. The Subject Person's manager (B) and employee (C) cannot generate case documents.

questions.stem: After configuration on a Lifecycle Event is complete, what additional configuration is needed to initiate the LE process for an employee?

options.text: None. The LE will automatically trigger based on its configuration
An Event is needed to initiate the LE process
A Scheduled Job is needed to initiate the LE process
An HR Service is needed to initiate the LE process

questions.explanation: After configuring a Lifecycle Event, an HR Service is needed to initiate the LE process for an employee. The HR Service acts as the entry point — when a case is created via the HR Service (either through the Employee Service Center or manually by HR), the system triggers the associated Lifecycle Event. Without an HR Service, there is no mechanism to start the LE.

questions.stem: In Employee Document Management, which of the following statements is true for legal holds?

options.text: Legal Holds are permanent and cannot be removed
Legal Holds may be placed on a group of HR profiles
Legal Holds may be placed on either a Document Type or an individual employee’s HR Profile
Legal Holds may be manually placed on individual employee documents

questions.explanation: In Employee Document Management, Legal Holds may be placed on either a Document Type or an individual employee's HR Profile. Placing a hold on a Document Type prevents all documents of that type from being purged or edited across all employees. Placing it on an HR Profile prevents any documents for that specific employee from being purged. Legal holds can be removed (A is wrong).

questions.stem: Each HR service created in _______ has a corresponding transform map job.
questions.explanation: Each HR service created in HR Integration Service has a corresponding transform map job. The HR Integration Service defines the connection between ServiceNow and external HR systems, and each service configuration generates a transform map that handles the data mapping and transformation when records are imported or synchronized.

questions.stem: If the Workflow editor is utilized for a Lifecycle Event, how does the system know when a task or approval should be triggered?

options.text: The activity set trigger condition determines when it is triggered
Activities are automatically triggered on specific dates
The Activity trigger condition determines when it is triggered

questions.explanation: When using the Workflow editor for a Lifecycle Event, the activity set trigger condition determines when a task or approval is triggered. Each activity set has a trigger condition (Immediate, Date, Other Activity Sets, Advanced, Condition, or Combination) that defines when its activities become active. The activity set level, not individual activities, controls the timing.

questions.stem: What Primary Security aspects are focused on for the HR application? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The three primary security aspects for the HR application are: Contextual Security (C) which uses ACLs and data context to control record-level access, Roles and Groups (E) which control module and application access, and Platform Access (F) which covers authentication and instance access. Password Security (A) and Physical Security (D) are not HRSD-specific security focuses.

questions.stem:
A customer using Lifecycle Events Enterprise has configured their onboarding process. Now, management has tasked the HR Admin with creating a way to back out onboarding work in case the new employee decides not to join the company.
Which of these is the best method to use to reverse work already performed as part of this Lifecycle Event?

options.text: Check the “allow blackout” box on each of the activities
Configure a new Lifecycle Event with the necessary activities
Configure the rescind activity set with the necessary activities
Check the “allow blackout” box on each of the activity sets

questions.explanation: The rescind activity set is used to reverse work already performed as part of a Lifecycle Event. When a new employee decides not to join, the HR Admin configures rescind activities that can cancel tasks, revert provisioning, and notify departments. The rescind process is built into the lifecycle event builder and is enabled via the Enable Rescind button.

questions.stem: If the Applies to all services box is not checked on the COE ACL Configuration record, what additional configurations must be made to the record?

options.text: More than one group must be added to the Groups list
At least one HR Service must be selected for the Services list
An Applies when condition must be created for each Service

questions.explanation: If the Applies to all services box is not checked on the COE ACL Configuration record, at least one HR Service must be selected for the Services list. This specifies which specific HR Services the access configuration applies to. Without checking the apply-all box, you must explicitly list which services the group access rules cover.

questions.stem: If an HR Document must be manually generated for an HR Case, who is able to generate the document from the Case record?

options.text: Only an HR Admin can generate Documents from a Case
Any HR professional can generate the Document, even if they are not assigned to the Case
Only the assigned to person can manually generate Documents from a Case
Only the Manager of the assignment group can generate the Document

questions.explanation: Only the assigned to person can manually generate Documents from an HR Case. This ensures document generation is controlled by the responsible agent, maintaining proper accountability. Other HR professionals, even HR Admins or group managers, cannot generate documents for cases they are not assigned to when manual generation is required.

questions.stem: What role is required at a minimum, to access the Lifecycle Events Cases View Dashboard?
questions.explanation: The LE Admin [sn_hr_le.admin] role is required at minimum to access the Lifecycle Events Cases View Dashboard. This dashboard provides lifecycle event case management views and reporting, which requires lifecycle events administration access. HR Basic (A) and Case Reader (B) provide insufficient access, while HR Admin (D) may have access but through the inherited LE Admin role.

questions.stem: Using the Lifecycle Event Enterprise application, tasks may only be assigned to... (Choose the most appropriate answer.)

options.text: Only users with a Client Role
Only users with an HR role
HR Case Workers. Employees, users in other groups
Only users with the Manager role

questions.explanation: Using Lifecycle Events Enterprise, tasks may be assigned to HR Case Workers, Employees, and users in other groups across the organization. This is the key differentiator of LE Enterprise vs standard LE — it enables cross-departmental tasking beyond just the HR department, allowing onboarding tasks to be assigned to IT, facilities, security, and other teams.

questions.stem: What identifies data from HRSD to push to a third-party HR application?
questions.explanation: HR Outbound Schema Mapping identifies data from HRSD to push to a third-party HR application. Outbound mappings define which ServiceNow fields are sent to external systems and how they map to the target system's schema. Inbound Schema Mapping (A) handles data coming into ServiceNow, not going out.

questions.stem: When configuring the Onboarding Lifecycle Event, the HR Admin did not select an Audience for the 'Select a Desk' task. If a remote employee is being onboarded. how does the system handle this task?

options.text: The Lifecycle Event rescind process will be triggered
The Lifecycle Event will be canceled
The activity will be triggered and must be manually closed

questions.explanation: When no Audience is set on a Lifecycle Event activity, the activity triggers for all employees regardless of their attributes. So if a remote employee is onboarded and the 'Select a Desk' task has no audience filter, the activity will be triggered and must be manually closed since it applies to everyone. The activity is not automatically skipped when no audience is configured.

questions.stem: When configuring a record on the COE ACL Configuration module how can you apply the conditions to all HR services for the COE?

options.text: Add a filter condition for each HR service
Select the Applies to all services box
Write a new ACL record for each HR service
Select each HR service using the Services list

questions.explanation: To apply conditions to all HR services for a COE on the COE ACL Configuration record, select the Applies to all services box. This checkbox applies the access configuration universally to every HR service within that COE, eliminating the need to individually select each service. Without it, you must manually add services to the Services list.

questions.stem: If you have both Admin [admin] and HR Admin [sn_hr_core.admin] roles and want to configure an Access Control Rule for the HR Payroll table, which of the following must first be done?

options.text: Manually add the Delegated Developer role to your User record
Manually add the security_admin role to your User record
From the User dropdown in the banner, elevate your role to delegated_developer
From the User dropdown in the banner, elevate your role to security_admin

questions.explanation: To configure an ACL for the HR Payroll table with Admin and HR Admin roles, you must elevate to security_admin from the User dropdown in the banner. ACL configuration always requires the elevated security_admin role regardless of other roles. Delegated developer (A, C) and manually adding security_admin (B) are not the correct approaches — elevation via the banner is the standard process.

questions.stem: The customer has a group of developers who will be tasked with making subprod updates to the HR Integrations application. Customer policy states these developers cannot be granted the System Administrator [admin] role. Which of these is the best solution for granting the appropriate access needed to complete development work m the HR application?

options.text: Grant them delegated developer role to the global application scope
Advise the customer this work must be completed in Production
Grant them delegated developer role only to the HR Integrations application scope
Submit an exception request to allow them to have the Admin role

questions.explanation: Grant the developers the delegated developer role scoped only to the HR Integrations application scope. This follows the principle of least privilege — they get development access within the HR Integrations scope without admin or broader access.
